newsitem.title: USA: US Airways could furlough pilots June 30.
newsitem.headline: US Airways could furlough pilots June 30.

text.p: US Airways Group Inc could begin to furlough, or lay off, pilots when a no-furlough agreement expires on June 30, the pilots union said.
As part of a 1992 contract agreement that demanded wage concessions from the pilots, the airline agreed not to furlough any pilots until the summer of 1997, the union said.

US Airways could not be reached for comment on whether it would begin to cut pilots, but the The Washington Post reported that US Airways' board plans to furlough workers unless unless a last-minute agreement is reached with employees on cutting costs.
US Airways currently has 283 pilots on furlough, the union said. Additional pilots could be furloughed starting June 30.

"I am very disappointed that management has chosen to threaten US Airways employees and their families as a part of its negotiations strategy," said Jon Bryan, chairman of the US Airways unit of the Air Line Pilots Association. US Airways has struggled with labor talks with its pilots since the June 1992 contract became amendable on April, 30, 1996.
US Airways, the nation's sixth largest airline, has said it may need to cut service on unprofitable routes and reduce the size of the airline if it does not achieve a "competitive cost structure."
The airline also may cancel a pending order for up to 400 Airbus Industrie aircraft if it cannot cut costs by September 30, the union said.

US Airways' returned to profitability in the first quarter and topped Wall Street expectations. The airline, however, said it suffered losses in key markets due to its high cost structure and increased competition from low-cost rivals.
The pilots and the company are expected to resume contract negotiations this week. While the airline said talks have continued without progress, the pilots union said the two sides has made strides.
"The pilots agree with management in more areas than we disagree," said Mark Thorpe, a media representative for the pilots union.
